facts.raw_span: A 62-year-old woman
IgG kappa plasma cell myeloma (Durie-Salmon IIA, R-ISS II)
previously treated with multiple chemotherapy regimens, two autologous stem-cell transplants, thalidomide maintenance, and focal bone radiotherapy
asymptomatic with stable vital signs
no hepatosplenomegaly on examination
Liver function tests, including ALT, AST, ALP, GGTP, and bilirubin, were within normal limits
a 35 mm lesion in the right hepatic lobe showed an SUVmax of 6.1
a 17 mm lesion in segment VI with moderately increased T2 signal, decreased T1 signal, weak heterogeneous contrast enhancement, and restricted diffusion
favoring a non-characteristic malignant lesion
Serial imaging over subsequent months showed a decrease in lesion size to 10 mm, followed by enlargement to 57 × 46 mm
a percutaneous liver biopsy was planned to establish a definitive diagnosis
